name: Subordinate Closed Interrogative with if

1.definition: Introduces a closed question in licensed complement positions.

relatedConstructions.notes: Asked if Jo was ready embeds a question. If Jo was ready, we could leave makes readiness a condition on the main clause.

projection.target: The clause has embedded question interpretation and ordinary subject–verb order. In this use if cannot introduce a whether-to infinitival.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Questions inside sentences with if
curious.summary: After a verb like wonder or ask, if can introduce a question that the sentence reports.
curious.body: In I wondered if Lee had arrived, the question is whether Lee had arrived, but it's tucked inside the sentence. The sentence reports a question rather than asking one. The words inside keep an ordinary order, with the subject before the verb. This if is different from the if of a condition. Asked if Jo was ready reports a question. In If Jo was ready, we could leave, readiness is a condition on the main clause.
curious.try: Say I wondered if Lee had arrived. Now say If Lee had arrived, we could start. In which sentence does the if introduce a question?

teacher.summary: Useful for separating if that introduces an embedded question from conditional if, and for contrasting if with whether.
teacher.explain: Interrogative if introduces a finite subordinate closed interrogative clause in licensed complement positions. The embedded clause has embedded-question interpretation and ordinary subject-verb order. Conditional if is different: in If Jo was ready, we could leave, the if-clause makes readiness a condition on the main clause. Interrogative if cannot introduce a whether-to infinitival.
teacher.terms: Subordinate closed interrogative: an embedded yes/no question. Compare whether, which is related; see this dictionary's entry on whether.

contrasts.text: They asked if Jo was ready.
If Jo was ready, we could leave.

watch_for: A learner might read the if in asked if Jo was ready as a condition.
A learner might expect if to introduce a to-infinitival the way whether can.
teacher.activity: Give students sentences with if. They sort them into embedded question (asked if Jo was ready) and condition (If Jo was ready, we could leave) and say how they decided.

checked.note: Fixed: removed 'only on that condition' (stronger than the entry's 'a condition on the main clause'); try question now says the if introduces a question; the whether-to infinitival restriction is stated of interrogative if explicitly. Dismissed: none.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Subordinate Closed Interrogative with if." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/closed-interrogative-if-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
